reasons.C: Long semicolon-linked accumulating sentences, an extended figurative simile, a rhetorical question and an earnest, elegiac Edwardian register closest to the passage's movement and stance.
reasons.A: Right period diction and semicolon-chained, cumulative rhythm with the 'one has only to' turn, but plainer and less figurative than the passage, with a more cautious hedged close.
reasons.B: Shorter, modern declarative sentences, few semicolons and a conversational register ('It did, of course'); least like the passage's rolling cadence and period feel.
